original_question: Does the blow-up of a Hirzebruch surface at four general points have pseudo-effective tangent bundle, and what can be said about blow-ups of Hirzebruch surfaces at special points?
target_in_paper: Section 4, Problem 4.6: the remaining problem in the classification of surfaces with pseudo-effective tangent bundle.
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the exact open problem almost verbatim: it names the right class of surfaces (blow-ups of Hirzebruch surfaces), the unresolved general case (four general blow-up points), the correct positivity property (pseudo-effective tangent bundle), and the paper's follow-up question about special blow-up centers.
missing_details: The paper is working over the complex numbers and in the category of smooth projective varieties; here the objects are smooth projective surfaces over \mathbb{C}.
The surface should be specified explicitly as X, the blow-up of a Hirzebruch surface \mathbb{F}_e=\mathbb{P}_{\mathbb{P}^1}(\mathcal{O}\oplus\mathcal{O}(e)) for some e\ge 0, at the chosen points.
The quantifier over Hirzebruch surfaces is implicit in the draft: the problem is asked for blow-ups of Hirzebruch surfaces in general, not for one fixed \mathbb{F}_e.

The phrase "pseudo-effective tangent bundle" should be made stand-alone by using the paper's definition from Proposition 4.1; equivalently, there should exist an ample line bundle A such that A\otimes \operatorname{Sym}^m T_X is generated by global sections at a general point for every integer m>0.
The phrase "four general points" should be tied explicitly to the blow-up centers on the Hirzebruch surface.
The phrase "special points" is not fully stand-alone unless rephrased as special configurations of blow-up centers on the Hirzebruch surface.
To match the paper's intent exactly, it helps to note that this is posed as the remaining problem in the classification of surfaces with pseudo-effective tangent bundle.
The paper notes immediately before Problem 4.6 that its notion of pseudo-effectivity is the stronger one from Proposition 4.1, not the weaker notion used in the cited work of Höring-Liu-Shao.
refined_question: Over \mathbb{C}, let \mathbb{F}_e be a Hirzebruch surface and let X be the blow-up of \mathbb{F}_e at four general points. Does the smooth projective surface X have pseudo-effective tangent bundle T_X? More generally, what can be said about the pseudo-effectivity of T_X when the blow-up centers on \mathbb{F}_e form a special configuration?
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently, by Proposition 4.1, for such a blow-up X is there an ample line bundle A on X such that A\otimes \operatorname{Sym}^m T_X is generated by global sections at a general point of X for every integer m>0? Likewise, what can be said about this condition for blow-ups at special configurations of points on a Hirzebruch surface?
justification: The draft is essentially a near-verbatim restatement of the paper's Problem 4.6. In the introduction, the author says that Section 4 focuses on pseudo-effective tangent bundles and the differences from the nef case. Section 4 then fixes the paper's notion of pseudo-effectivity via Proposition 4.1, gives the surrounding structure theorem in Theorem 4.2, and finally states as "the remaining problem in the classification of surfaces" the two-part question about blow-ups of Hirzebruch surfaces at four general points and at special points. I therefore kept the scope exactly at that open problem and only added the ambient complex-projective setting, the implicit quantifier over Hirzebruch surfaces, and a stand-alone formulation of the pseudo-effectivity condition.
